Occasionally a player may be missing from the Player Pool due to trades or other unforeseen circumstances. Each player listed in the player pool has an assigned salary and a valid lineup must not exceed the salary cap of $50,000. Due to the fluid nature of rosters, in the event a team adjusts their roster after player pools are finalized, DraftKings reserves the right to adjust player pools after contests for that Game Set have become available. In these instances, additional players may be added to the Player Pool up until 48 hours before a Game Set’s lock. This may result in valid lineups becoming invalid. Any participants who have entered contests for the Game Set prior to the adjustment will be notified via email. A "Game Set" is a set of games used for contests; each contest is tied to one Game Set. Contests tied to the same Game Set can be created at different times. Therefore, game policies are based on the timing of a Game Set being made available, not each individual contest. ### Position Eligibility Player positions are determined at the sole discretion of DraftKings. ### Lineup Edits Lineups may be edited at any time leading up to games. Each individual player will become "locked" at the scheduled start time of their team’s game. A locked player cannot be added or removed from a roster spot. Locked roster spots for all entries are displayed in contest GameCenters. If the scheduled start time for a game changes after contests for a Game Set containing that game become available, DraftKings will take measures to ensure the change is reflected on Draft Screens and for lineup editing purposes. In the rare case that a game starts before the scheduled start time, all players within that game will become locked as soon as our feed reflects that the game has begun. Additionally, any swaps that were made after the real-life start time of the game will result in those lineups being disqualified and refunded. ### Cancelled, Postponed, and Rescheduled Games In the event that a game is cancelled or postponed & rescheduled to a time within the original Scoring Period and this change is made less than 24 hours before a Game Set’s start, the game will be included in the Game Set and players listed to play in that game will be eligible to accrue points. If a game is rescheduled for a time OUTSIDE the original Scoring Period and this change is made less than 24 hours before a Game Set’s start, the game will be disabled from the Game Set and players listed to play in that game will NOT be eligible to accrue point. Players who you selected for your roster as of the time of the lock of the disabled game will remain in your roster and will accrue zero points. Players in disabled games will become locked at the originally scheduled start time of their game. The Scoring Period for NFL is defined as the timeframe between the scheduled start of the first game within the Game Set and 11:59pm ET on the first Wednesday after the last scheduled game within the Game Set. In the event that a game is cancelled or postponed & rescheduled to any time (both outside & within the original Scoring Period) and this change is made MORE than 24 hours before a Game Set’s start, it is at the sole discretion of Draftkings to include or remove the game from that given Game Set. In the event a game is postponed, Draftkings will make a decision no later than 11:59pm ET of the day of the game on how to handle the postponed game. Any games that are disabled will be indicated as such on Draft Screens. Emails and other notifications may also be used to notify users of disabled games. Games are "known" to be canceled or postponed once their status is updated as such by DraftKings’ NFL stats-provider, STATS LLC. ## Biography

**CAREER HIGHLIGHTS**

- **First-Team AP All-Pro**: 2023, 2024
- **Second-Team AP All-Pro**: 2025
- **Pro Bowl:** 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025
- **NFC Offensive Player of the Week**: 2022 (Week 2)
- **NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month**: 2021 (December)
- **Pepsi NFL Rookie of the Week:** 2021 (Week 18)
- Owns the most receptions (547) through five-career seasons in NFL history
- Is the only player in NFL history to record at least 90 receptions in each of their first five-career seasons, and the only player in NFL history to produce 100 receptions in four of a player's first five-career seasons.
- Became the fifth player in NFL history to produce 100 catches in four-straight seasons and the fourth player in NFL history to top 100 receptions and 10 touchdown receptions in three-straight seasons.
- Owns the most 100-catch seasons (four) in franchise history.
- Is the second player in NFL history to have 500 receptions, 6,000 receiving yards and 40 touchdowns through five-career seasons.
- Became the third player in NFL history to notch 115 receptions and 10 receiving touchdowns in consecutive seasons.
- Became the fourth player in NFL history to notch 110 receptions in three-straight seasons.
- Has the most 90-reception seasons (five) and 100-reception seasons (four) in Lions history.
- Is the only player in franchise history to have 100 receptions and 10 receiving touchdowns in consecutive seasons.
- Ties for the NFL's third-longest streak with eight-straight games recording a receiving touchdown (Weeks 3-11 of 2024).
- Owns the NFL record for most consecutive games (six) with eight receptions and a touchdown
- Joined Herman Moore (Oct. 29, 1995) as the only Lions players since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to produce a game with at least 120 scrimmage yards and three receiving touchdowns vs. the Bears (9/14/2025).
- Currently ranks third in receptions (547), fourth in receiving yards (6,252), third in receiving touchdowns (44), third in 100-yard receiving yard games (24) and second in 10-reception games (10) through five-career seasons in franchise history.
- Joined Calvin Johnson (2011-13) and Herman Moore (1995-97) as the only Lions wideouts to earn multiple First-Team AP All-Pro selections in 2024. He also joined Johnson and Moore as the only receivers in team history to earn three-straight Pro Bowl berths.
- Joined Davante Adams (2020-21) and Antonio Brown (2014-15) as the only players in NFL history to produce 115 receptions and 10 receiving touchdowns in consecutive seasons.
- Produced 11 games with a touchdown reception in 2024, tying Calvin Johnson (2011) for the most games in a season in team history.
- Joined Larry Fitzgerald as the only players in NFL history to log multiple seasons with 100 receptions, 1,000 receiving yards and 10 receiving touchdowns through four-career seasons.
- Set his single-game career high in receiving yards (193) and set a career high and tied the franchise record for receptions with 14 vs. Buffalo (12/15/24).
- Produced a receiving touchdown in eight-straight games in 2024 (Weeks 3-11), tying for the third-longest streak in NFL history.
- At 23 years old in 2022, St. Brown became the youngest player in franchise history to record 100 receptions and 1,000 receiving yards in a single season. He became the first player in Lions history to produce 900-plus receiving yards in each their first two NFL seasons (2021-22).
- Tied the NFL record for the longest streak of games (eight) with at least eight receptions from 2021-22.
- Set Lions rookie records for receptions (90) and receiving yards (912). His receptions were the most a first-year NFL player not selected within the first three rounds of a draft has had.
- Registered his first career two-touchdown receiving performance as he posted nine receptions for 116 yards (12.9 avg.) vs. Washington (9/18/22). He became the third WR in NFL history to produce a game with 100 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, and 50 rushing yards.
- Became the first rookie wide receiver in franchise history to record a walk-off touchdown, doing so vs. Minnesota (12/11/21).
- Became the third wide receiver in NFL history to produce a game with a rushing touchdown, receiving touchdown and a two-point conversion in Week 17 at Seattle (1/2/22).

**COLLEGE**

- Played at USC from 2018-20, totaling 178 receptions for 2,270 yards (12.8 avg.) and 16 touchdowns in that span. He left the program ranked 11th in receptions and added seven-career 100-yard games.
- **2020:** Had a team-best 41 receptions for 478 yards (11.7 avg.) and a team-high seven touchdown receptions in six games (all starts).
- First-Team All-Pac-12
- Team Captain
- **2019:** Played in all 13 games (12 starts) and tallied 77 receptions for 1,042 yards (13.5 avg.) and six touchdowns.
- Had four 100-yard games
- His 77 receptions rank 12th in a single-season in USC history
- **2018:** Appeared in all 12 games (five starts) and had a team-best 60 receptions for 750 yards (12.5 avg.) and three touchdowns.
- Honorable-Mention Pac-12 Freshman Offensive Player of the Year

**PERSONAL**

- Attended Mater Dei High School in Santa Ana, Calif.
- His full name is Amon-Ra Julian Heru J. St. Brown. He was named after the Egyptian sun god (Amon-Ra) and the Egyptian sky god (Heru).
- Is fluent in German and French, having spent time living in both countries.
- His father, John Brown, was a bodybuilder who won two Mr. Universe and three Mr. World titles in the 1980s.
- Brother, Equanimeous, is a receiver for the New Orleans Saints.

As a sophomore, earned Academic All-Big Ten honors. Played in 12 games and registered 1 recept. for 25 yds. In 2013, played in 12 games and recorded 5 recepts. for 108 yds. Also earned Academic All-Big Ten honors. Redshirted in 2012.

#### AWARDS & HONORS:

- 2018: AP Second-Team All-Pro, PFWA NFL Most Improved Player, PFWA All-NFC Team, Bill Walsh Award, NFC Pro Bowl, 49ers Community Relations Veteran Player Award
- 2019: AP First-Team All-Pro, PFWA All-NFL Team, PFWA All-NFC Team, Len Eshmont Award, NFC Pro Bowl
- 2021: NFC Offensive Player of the Week (Week 14), NFC Pro Bowl, PFWA All-NFC Team, 49ers NFL Salute to Service Award Nominee
- 2022: NFC Pro Bowl Games, AP Second-Team All-Pro, PFWA All-NFC Team, NFL Salute to Service Award Finalist
- 2023: NFC Pro Bowl, AP First-Team All-Pro, PFWA All-NFC Team
- 2024: NFC Pro Bowl, AP Second-Team All-Pro, Len Eshmont Award, Garry Niver Award, NFL Salute to Service Award

#### NFL:

- Kittle is the all-time leader in rec. yds. (7,380) by a 49ers TE and ranks 3rd among all players in franchise history (WR Jerry Rice - 19,247; WR Terrell Owens - 8,572).
- Has registered 4 seasons with 1,000-or-more rec. yds., making him 1 of 5 tight ends in NFL history to register 4 seasons with 1,000-ormore rec. yds. in a career (TE Travis Kelce, KC - 7; TE Tony Gonzalez, KC - 4; TE Rob Gronkowski, NE - 4; TE Jason Witten, Dal. - 4).
- Kittle's 4 seasons with 1,000-or-more rec. yds. are the most by a 49ers TE and rank 3rd-most among all players in franchise history.
- Since entering the NFL in 2017, Kittle ranks 2nd in rec. yds. among all TEs (7,380).
- Reached 7,074 career rec. yds. in 109 games, surpassing former TE Antonio Gates (119 games) as the 3rd-fastest TE to reach 7,000 career rec. yds. in NFL history.
- Reached 6,065 career rec. yds. in 95 games, surpassing former TE Jimmy Graham (100 games) as the 4th-fastest TE to reach 6,000 career rec. yds. in NFL history
- Kittle became the fastest 49ers TE to reach 6,000 career rec. yds. and the 3rd-fastest 49ers player to reach 6,000 career rec. yds.
- Kittle also became the 5th tight end in NFL history to register 6,000-or-more rec. yds. in the first 7 seasons of his career (TE Travis Kelce; TE Jimmy Graham; TE Antonio Gates; TE Rob Gronkowski).
- Surpassed 5,000 career rec. yds. in 79 career games, the 4th-fewest games to reach 5,000 career rec. yds. by a TE in NFL history.
- Surpassed 4,000 career rec. yds. in 61 career games, which is tied for the 2nd-fewest games to reach 4,000 career rec. yds. by a TE in NFL history (TE Kellen Winslow Sr., SD - 58 games; TE Rob Gronkowski, NE - 61 games).
- Surpassed 3,000 career rec. yds. in 47 career games, which is tied for the 2nd-fewest games to reach 3,000 career rec. yds. by a TE in NFL history (TE Kellen Winslow Sr., SD - 45 games; TE Rob Gronkowski, NE - 47 games).
- His 3,380 rec. yds. through his first 50 career games are the 3rd-most by a TE in NFL history.
- In 2018, set an NFL record at the time for most rec. yds. (1,377) in a season by a TE. His 1,377 rec. yds. now rank as the 2nd-most in a single season by a TE in NFL history (TE Travis Kelce, KC - 1,416 rec. yds. in 2020).
- Has 21 career 100-yd. games, which are the most by a TE in franchise history and rank 3rd-most among all players (WR Jerry Rice - 65; WR Terrell Owens - 25).
- Is the 6th player and only TE in franchise history to record multiple 1,000-yd. seasons (2018-19 & 2023-24).
- Registered 7 recepts. for a career-high 210 yds. and 1 TD vs. Den. (12/9/18). His 210 rec. yds. are the most in a single game by a 49ers TE and rank as the 8th-most in a single game in franchise history.
- With 210 rec. yds. vs. Den. (12/9/18), he became the first 49ers TE to eclipse the 1,000-yd. receiving mark and set the franchise record for most yds. in a single season by a 49ers TE. At the time, he was the first member of the 49ers to register at least 1,000 rec. yds. in a single season since WR Anquan Boldin registered 1,062 rec. yds. in 2014.

# 49ers Rule Out Mike Evans vs. Falcons; Christian Kirk Questionable Ahead of Week 7 \#SFvsATL

Oct 23, 2026 at 03:02 PM

![Author Image](https://static.clubs.nfl.com/image/upload/t_thumb_squared/t_lazy/f_auto/v1778628932/49ers/fb3jkuz2asmaux1n4xhp.jpg)

[Brooke Evans](https://www.49ers.com/author/brooke-evans)

Digital Editor

[Opens Twitter profile page in new window - Opens new window](https://x.com/brookeevansss)[Opens Instagram profile page in new window - Opens new window](https://www.instagram.com/brooke.evans/?hl=en)

- Copied!

The San Francisco 49ers wrapped up their final practice of the week ahead of their Week 7 road matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Following Friday's practice, head coach Kyle Shanahan ruled out WR [Mike Evans](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/mike-evans/ "Mike Evans") (ribs, Achilles), WR [Deebo Samuel Sr.](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/deebo-samuel/ "Deebo Samuel Sr.") (hamstring), DL [Nick Bosa](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/nick-bosa/ "Nick Bosa") (knee/calf), LB [Luke Gifford](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/luke-gifford/ "Luke Gifford") (groin), S [Marques Sigle](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/marques-sigle/ "Marques Sigle") (ankle), and LB [Garret Wallow](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/garret-wallow/ "Garret Wallow") (hamstring) for Sunday's game.

WR [Christian Kirk](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/christian-kirk/ "Christian Kirk") (calf), DB [Siran Neal](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/siran-neal/ "Siran Neal") (knee), and CB [Upton Stout](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/upton-stout/ "Upton Stout") (shoulder) are questionable.

**Questionable Players**

Kirk was a full participant in all three practices this week as he continues working towards his return. Offensive coordinator Klay Kubiak shared a positive update on the veteran receiver's progress Thursday.

"He looks good. We got him back into practice last week and you can see him getting better this week for sure," Kubiak said. "He's a guy who's been preparing mentally, so it's been impressive to see him step in and just be really sharp on the details."

Neal and Stout did not participate in Wednesday or Thursday's practices before returning to a limited session on Friday. Both defensive backs enter Sunday's matchup listed as questionable.

**Ruled-Out Players**

Evans has been ruled out after missing all three practices this week with rib and Achilles injuries. The veteran wide receiver exited San Francisco's Week 6 victory over Washington right before half after recording three receptions for 94 yards.

With Evans and Samuel Sr. sidelined, Kubiak expressed confidence in the receiving group and the opportunity for other players to step into larger roles like Kirk and WR [Jordan Watkins](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/jordan-watkins/ "Jordan Watkins").

"It's a big moment for those guys. If Mike's not able to go, then guys got to step up and we have full confidence in them," Kubiak said. "Mike's a heck of a player and he's been huge for us this year, but we're very confident in the people that we have going right now."

Bosa, Samuel Sr., Sigle, and Wallow remain sidelined after also missing San Francisco's Week 6 matchup against Washington.

Gifford has also been ruled out after missing all three practices this week with a groin injury.

**Returning / No Game Designation**

DL [Mykel Williams](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/mykel-williams/ "Mykel Williams") (knee) progressed throughout the week, going from a nonparticipant Wednesday to limited participation Thursday and full participation Friday.

S [Ashtyn Davis](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/ashtyn-davis/ "Ashtyn Davis") (hamstring) and LB [Jaden Dugger](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/jaden-dugger/ "Jaden Dugger") (knee) were limited Wednesday and Thursday before returning to full participation Friday.

DL [Romello Height](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/romello-height/ "Romello Height") (hand) was a full participant throughout the week, while T [Trent Williams](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/trent-williams/ "Trent Williams") returned to full participation Thursday and Friday after receiving a rest day Wednesday.

All five players carry no game designations heading into Sunday's matchup.

**Preparing for Atlanta**

The 49ers enter Week 7 with a 6-0 record following their 23-17 "Monday Night Football" victory over the Washington Commanders.

As San Francisco prepares for its first East Coast road trip of the season, Shanahan emphasized the importance of maintaining focus against a competitive Falcons team.

"When you turn on Atlanta's film, they know how big of a challenge this is," Shanahan said. "We got a number of guys down. We know they do too, but they're a team that their record doesn't show it, but they're a team that should be there in the end."

**Below is the complete Week 7 Status Report:**

- WR [Mike Evans](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/mike-evans/ "Mike Evans") (ribs, Achilles) - OUT
- WR [Deebo Samuel Sr.](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/deebo-samuel/ "Deebo Samuel Sr.") (hamstring) - OUT
- LB [Garret Wallow](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/garret-wallow/ "Garret Wallow") (hamstring) - OUT
- DL [Nick Bosa](https://www.49ers.com/team/players-roster/nick-bosa/ "Nick Bosa") (knee, calf) - OUT
